claim.pdf_says: Format 4 (into-remainder): DIVIDE { identifier-1 / literal-1 } INTO { identifier-2 / literal-2 } -- INTO printed on the middle line between the two two-row braces
claim.why_it_matters: Same layout defect as Format 2: INTO is drawn above the braces instead of between them, and the identifier-1/literal-1 brace is stretched with an empty upper portion, misrepresenting where INTO sits in the DIVIDE ... INTO ... GIVING ... REMAINDER format.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered PDF page 514 (printed p.490), Format 4 (into-remainder): one baseline reads DIVIDE, a two-row brace {identifier-1 / literal-1}, then INTO (underlined) at mid-height, then a two-row brace {identifier-2 / literal-2}; it matches Format 2 on the same page. The markdown page-514.md Format 4 block is quoted accurately in the claim: the first brace is stretched to five rows with two empty upper rows, INTO sits alone on the top row to the right of that brace, and the second brace starts two rows lower with no keyword between the braces. Format 1 and Format 3 on the same page are drawn correctly (DIVIDE {..} INTO/BY {..} on one baseline), so this is a defect, not a house convention. Reading order (DIVIDE, brace 1, INTO, brace 2) and the brace alternatives can still be recovered, so this is a structural figure defect and not a normative one: the syntax is unchanged, but the drawing misplaces INTO and distorts the first brace.
